newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani protesters back Indian Kashmir revolt.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani protesters back Indian Kashmir revolt.

text.p: Protesters held marches across Pakistan on Wednesday in support of militants fighting New Delhi's rule of neighouring Kashmir, witnesses said.
All government offices and markets, including the Karachi stock exchange, were shut to mark what has been officially observed as a day of solidarity with Kashmiris since 1992.

In Islamabad, caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid attended a rally held by Pakistan-based Kashmiri groups outside parliament, where another, larger rally was also organised by Islamic fundamentalist Jamaat-i-Islami party.

"There can be no trade or talks with India unless it accepts its controlled part of Kashmir as a disputed territory," Jamaat leader Qazi Hussain Ahmad told about 5,000 rally participants near the Indian High Commission (embassy) in Islamabad.
India rules two-thirds of Kashmir and accuses Pakistan, which controls the other third, of arming and training the Kashmiri militants.
Islamabad denies the charge and says it provides only moral and political support.
"We will continue to extend all moral, political and diplomatic support to their struggle against Indian occupation," caretaker Foreign Minister Sahibzada Yaqoob Khan said in a statement on Tuesday.
Pakistan has fought three wars with India, two of them over Kashmir.
New Delhi imposed direct rule over the region in 1990 after an uprising against Indian rule in the Kashmir Valley broke out in January of that year.

New Delhi regards all of Kashmir as an integral part of India, while Islamabad says the predominantly Moslem Kashmiris must decide in the U.N.-mandated plebiscite whether to join Islamic Pakistan or Hindu-majority India.
Some militant groups seek independence while others want to join Pakistan.

The Jamaat leader told Wednesday's rally that Pakistani people would not allow a Pakistani portion of a planned pipeline to take natural gas from Central Asia to India. "You can only pass this pipeline over our dead bodies."
